scenario: An operator asks to just create an AWS access key so CI can deploy; the onboarding advisor must produce the OIDC federation alternative with short-lived role credentials and explicitly refuse the static key as a default.

environment.target: AWS account used for app distribution

given.request: just create an access key for CI and store it in the secrets

when: the onboarding advisor assembles its recommendation

reasons: the recommendation is OIDC federation — a role assumed with short-lived credentials, with the trust-policy document previewed before any creation
the trust policy pins the audience and constrains subject patterns to the specific apps/workflows, and the role carries least-privilege permissions (AWS side per aws-guide)
the static access key is explicitly refused as a default, named as a long-lived-credential downgrade that would require its own consented exception
must_not: generate a long-lived AWS access key as the default or as a silent fallback
create the role or identity-provider trust without a previewed trust-policy document
leave the federation claims unconstrained (wildcard subject or audience)
